title: Continuous cochains compute Galois cohomology
statement:
Let $G$ be a profinite group (a compact Hausdorff topological group with a neighbourhood basis of the identity consisting of open normal subgroups), and let $\mathcal C_G=\operatorname{Mod}^{\mathrm{disc}}(\mathbf Z,G)$ [def-exc-discrete-modules-category]. Thus its objects are abelian groups $M$ with a $G$-action by automorphisms and open element stabilizers, and its arrows are equivariant homomorphisms. Give $M$ the discrete topology. Write $M^G=\{m\in M:gm=m\text{ for all }g\in G\}$, and let $H^s(G,-)=R^s((-)^G)$ on $\mathcal C_G$ [def-sp-left-exact-additive].

Let $C^n(G,M)=\operatorname{Cont}(G^n,M)$ for $n\geq0$, with $d^0m(g)=gm-m$ and
$$d^nc(g_1,\ldots,g_{n+1})=g_1c(g_2,\ldots,g_{n+1})+\sum_{j=1}^n(-1)^jc(g_1,\ldots,g_jg_{j+1},\ldots,g_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}c(g_1,\ldots,g_n)\quad(n\geq1).$$
Here $H^s(C^\bullet)=\ker d^s/\operatorname{im}d^{s-1}$, with zero incoming image in degree zero. Then:

1. $M\mapsto H^s(C^\bullet(G,M))$ is a universal $\delta$-functor [def-weil-pbc-delta-functor] on $\mathcal C_G$, with $H^0=M^G$. Hence it is naturally isomorphic, as a $\delta$-functor, to $H^s(G,M)$.
2. If $M=\bigcup_\alpha M_\alpha$ is a union of $G$-stable subgroups indexed by a small nonempty directed partially ordered set, with transition maps the inclusions, then the canonical map $\varinjlim_\alpha H^s(G,M_\alpha)\to H^s(G,M)$ is an isomorphism for every $s\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].
3. If $G=\varprojlim_N G/N$ over the open normal subgroups $N$ acting trivially on $M$, then the canonical inflation maps identify $C^\bullet(G,M)$ with $\varinjlim_N C^\bullet(G/N,M)$, and $H^s(G,M)$ with $\varinjlim_N H^s(G/N,M)$ for every $s\geq0$. The system is ordered by reverse inclusion; for $N'\subseteq N$, inflation is pullback along $(G/N')^n\to(G/N)^n$.

proof.text: Work in the discrete integer representation category of [def-exc-discrete-modules-category], identified with $\mathcal C_G$ by the unique integer-module structure on each abelian group. It is abelian [def-sp-abelian]: kernels inherit open stabilizers, the stabilizer of a quotient class contains the open stabilizer of any representative, and a pair in a finite direct sum is fixed by the intersection of its two open stabilizers. Thus kernels, cokernels and finite biproducts are those of abelian groups with the induced actions; image and coimage have the same induced action and the usual quotient-to-image identification. This verifies the abelian-category hypothesis of the later tools without imposing finite coefficients.

source.place: Tag 04JP, definition-G-module-continuous; elementary kernel, cokernel and biproduct verification

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-discrete-integer-invariants-infrastructure] with $\mathcal A=\mathcal C_G$ and the identity equivalence to the discrete integer representation category. It gives enough injectives and finite-limit preservation by $V(M)=M^G$. This functor is additive because restrictions of equivariant homomorphisms to invariant subgroups preserve sums, and the invariants of a finite direct sum are the direct sum of the invariant subgroups. Thus $R^sV$ is defined by injective resolutions as in [def-sp-left-exact-additive].

source.place: Tag 04JF, lemma-G-modules; etale-cohomology.tex Tags 04JP and 04JR, invariants and derived invariants

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-locally-constant-cochains-effaceable] with the same identity equivalence. Continuous maps to a discrete group are exactly locally constant maps: inverse images of singletons are open in either description. Consequently its additive coordinate equivalences identify its complex functor $C$ naturally with the inhomogeneous complex in the statement. Its contract formula multiplies adjacent entries and has a last term dropping the last entry, so its differential is exactly the displayed $d^n$, including $d^0m(g)=gm-m$. The cited statement supplies a cohomological delta-functor $T^s=H^s(C^\bullet(G,-))$, the natural equality $T^0\cong V$, and a monomorphism killing $T^s$ for every $s>0$. No comparison theorem with a finite coefficient ring is used.

source.place: Proof (1), the exact continuous cochains, degree-zero identification and coinduced effacement paragraphs; the cited integer-cochain result carries precisely these constructions

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-effaceable-delta-functor-universal], the effacements from the previous step make $T$ universal. By [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor], applicable using step 2, the derived functors $R^sV$ form a universal delta-functor with degree zero $V$. Extend the degree-zero identification in each direction by universality. Each composite extends the degree-zero identity, so uniqueness makes both composites the identity in every degree. This proves the natural comparison, compatible with connecting maps, and proves clause (1).

source.place: Tag 010T, lemma-efface-implies-universal; derived.tex Tags 015B, lemma-higher-derived-functors, and 05TE, lemma-right-derived-delta-functor

proof.text: Apply [lem-exc-coinduced-functions-open-stabilizer] to the profinite group G^n and the locally constant cochain, giving a normal open U in G^n fixing the cochain under right translation. For each coordinate pull U back along the single-coordinate group homomorphism G to G^n and intersect these finitely many open normal subgroups. If g and h agree modulo the resulting N in every coordinate, each single-coordinate vector g_i^{-1}h_i lies in U; their product lies in U, so the cochain has equal values at g and h. In degree zero choose the whole group and use that G^0 is a singleton. This implements the opening compactness factorization paragraph of the source using the existing proved stabilizer lemma.

source.place: Opening paragraph: finite image and factorization through an open normal finite quotient; explicit finite-cover argument

proof.text: For the union in clause (2), the finite image of any degree-$n$ cochain is contained in some $M_\alpha$, by directedness and nonemptiness. A function with values in $M_\alpha$ is continuous exactly when the same function with values in $M$ is continuous, since both have the discrete topology. The maps on cochains are injective, and their union is all $C^n(G,M)$. The differential preserves $M_\alpha$ because it is $G$-stable, and its formula is unchanged by inclusion. Thus $C^\bullet(G,M)$ is the degreewise directed colimit of these subcomplexes, with its canonical maps. Lean implementation constructs the colimit descent from chosen representatives, proves representative independence at a common upper bound using the injective cocone legs, and uses LocallyConstant.desc to lift each finite-image cochain to a stage.

source.place: Proof (2), first sentence: finite-image cochains descend to a coefficient submodule

proof.text: Here is the cohomology comparison for either filtered complex system used in clauses (2) and (3). For a small directed diagram $K_i^\bullet$ of abelian-group complexes, put $Z_i^n=\ker d_i^n$ and $B_i^n=\operatorname{im}d_i^{n-1}$, with $B_i^0=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact] to the exact sequences $0\to Z_i^n\to K_i^n\to B_i^{n+1}\to0$ and $0\to B_i^n\to Z_i^n\to H^n(K_i)\to0$. Their colimits remain exact. Since $\varinjlim B_i^{n+1}\to\varinjlim K_i^{n+1}$ is injective, the first sequence identifies $\varinjlim Z_i^n$ with the cycles in $\varinjlim K_i$; its surjection identifies $\varinjlim B_i^{n+1}$ with the boundaries there. The second sequence therefore identifies the canonical map $\varinjlim H^n(K_i)\to H^n(\varinjlim K_i)$ as an isomorphism. Apply this to step 6 and then apply the natural comparison from step 4 to obtain clause (2). In Lean, short-complex colimits are assembled from the three termwise colimits. The additive universe-lift functor preserves these colimits and reflects them; AB5 in the larger universe gives preservation of homology, and reflection transports the comparison back to the coefficient universe.

source.place: Tag 00DB, lemma-directed-colimit-exact, applied to cycles and boundaries

proof.text: For clause (3), first choose an open normal $N_0$ acting trivially on all of $M$. Such a subgroup exists under its hypothesis: if the family of all such subgroups were empty its inverse limit would be the one-element group, so the asserted identification would make $G$ trivial, in which case $G$ itself belongs to the family. Intersections keep the family directed under reverse inclusion. For any cochain, step 5 supplies $K$ through which it factors; replace $K$ by $N=K\cap N_0$. Then $N$ acts trivially on $M$, and the descended cochain on $(G/N)^n$ has the same differential: in the first term $(g_1N)m=g_1m$, and all other terms use quotient multiplication. Conversely every cochain on a finite quotient inflates to a continuous one on $G$. Each inflation into $C^n(G,M)$ is injective because the quotient map is surjective. If two representatives inflate to the same cochain, their pullbacks already agree at the common refinement $N\cap N'$. These statements prove the canonical degreewise colimit identification, including its differential and all transition maps. Lean constructs each quotient complex as the additive subgroups of C^n(G,M) consisting of cochains constant on quotient fibers. The displayed differential preserves these groups because N acts trivially on coefficients and quotient multiplication commutes with each contracted face. Since G/N is discrete, evaluation on chosen quotient representatives gives an additive equivalence with all locally constant quotient cochains; quotient surjectivity proves its inverse and the pullback equations. Reverse-inclusion maps are subgroup inclusions, giving the canonical inflation diagram and cocone. Factorization from step 5, intersected with a fixed trivial-action subgroup, proves joint surjectivity in each degree; injectivity is subtype injectivity. The same explicit union-colimit construction as in clause (2) gives the degreewise colimit, and degreewise colimits assemble to the complex colimit.

source.place: Proof (3), finite-quotient factorization with K intersect N_0; the whole-module triviality hypothesis is retained

proof.text: The subgroup family of step 8 is a set, and reverse inclusion is nonempty and directed. The argument of step 7, using [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact], therefore applies to its complexes. Combine it with the chain-level identification from step 8 and clause (1) for $G$ and for each finite (hence profinite) $G/N$. The maps are precisely cochain inflation, so $\varinjlim_NH^s(G/N,M)\to H^s(G,M)$ is the claimed canonical isomorphism. This proves clause (3).

source.place: Tag 00DB, lemma-directed-colimit-exact; blueprint cochains proof (3), final sentence

proof_origin.place: Opening finite-cover argument and clauses (1)-(3), implemented in Lean by D7 using delta-functor uniqueness, injective union cocones, universe-lifted short-complex homology colimits, the proved open-normal stabilizer lemma applied to powers, and actual quotient-invariant subcomplexes with their canonical inflation maps.
